article.story: MINNEAPOLIS -- — Isaac Asuma scored 21 points, and Kyan Evans had 16 points and 10 assists as Minnesota rolled past Western Illinois 99-63 on Monday. The Golden Gophers (5-0) shot 74.1% from the field in the first half, making 20 of 27 shots and 10 of 17 from 3-point range to build a 54-27 lead at the break. Minnesota opened the game with nine straight points and led 18-6 after Nolan Groves’ layup with 13:16 left. The Gophers continued pulling away behind Asuma and Evans, who combined for seven first-half 3-pointers. Evans hit a 3-pointer with 1:38 remaining, and Nolen Anderson followed with another from beyond the arc before Malick Kordel’s dunk sent Minnesota into halftime with a 27-point advantage. Asuma finished 8 of 11 from the field and added seven assists. Jaylen Crocker-Johnson had 11 points and nine rebounds, while Kordel scored 12 off the bench. Minnesota shot 67% overall, made 15 3-pointers and finished with 32 assists on 39 field goals. Jack Riley led Western Illinois (1-4) with 14 points. Daivion Traylor added 10. Up next Minnesota: Hosts Oklahoma State on Friday. Western Illinois: Plays UAlbany at home this Friday. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
